Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval. Compare the target with the middle element, then discard the half that cannot contain it. Maintain explicit bounds and update them so that every iteration makes progress. An iterative implementation requires only constant auxiliary space. Careful boundary tests should include an empty array, one element, duplicated values, and targets outside the stored range.

A graphics processor executes many lightweight threads together. Efficient kernels consider memory access patterns, synchronization, and the amount of work assigned to each thread. Adjacent threads should often access adjacent data. Registers are fast but limited, and excessive register use can reduce occupancy. Profiling should distinguish computation from memory transfer and host dispatch overhead before selecting an optimization.

Quantization represents values using fewer bits. A group of weights can share a scale and an offset, while each weight stores a small integer code. Dequantization reconstructs an approximation rather than the original value. Lower precision reduces storage but can introduce error. Calibration data helps estimate which operations are sensitive, and held-out evaluation checks whether local approximations preserve useful model behavior.

Network protocols separate responsibilities across layers. A reliable transport detects missing data and arranges retransmission, while an application defines the meaning of messages. Timeouts and retries should be bounded. Repeated requests may require idempotency keys to avoid duplicated side effects. Testing a service should include delayed responses, malformed messages, disconnected peers, and recovery after a process restarts.
